Thanks Hannah — quick technical clarifications and proposed language for the questionnaire items about measurement and attribution.

On measurement points and sampling
- We measure availability and latency at the service egress point (the edge return time recorded in our gateway) for customer-facing inference endpoints. This represents the time from request egress at our API fabric to the first response byte.
- Latency percentiles are calculated on a per-customer, per-region rolling 30-day window. Percentiles we report: P50, P95, P99. We also produce a P99.9 tail bucket for long-tail monitoring but P99 is the contractual metric.
- We normalize latency by a standard prompt footprint (32 tokens / typical LLM request). For customers serving significantly longer sequences we offer separate measurement buckets — call these "sequence-length-normalized" metrics — to avoid penalizing larger prompt workloads.
- Sampling: production telemetry is primarily full-sample for 200ms+ responses; for high-throughput customers we apply deterministic sampler based on request hash to cap telemetry ingestion. Sampling rules are consistent and applied before percentile computation (we adjust percentiles using Horvitz–Thompson weighting so sampled percentiles remain unbiased).

On synthetic probes and exclusion rules
- Synthetic probes (external synthetic checker requests) are logged separately and excluded from contractual SLO windows. We use them for alerting and regression detection, not contractual measurement.
- Maintenance windows: Planned maintenance windows >15 min that are scheduled with customer notification are excluded if they fall within the agreed maintenance SLA. Emergency maintenance or software rollbacks are not automatically excluded; we evaluate on a case-by-case basis with incident postmortems.

On attribution and multi-layer failures
- Attribution policy: We attribute a failure to Redwood if our edge telemetry shows 5xx responses or internal timeouts originating inside our inference runtime or gateway. If the outgoing path to a customer's VPC or private endpoint is failing (customer-controlled network or customer-side infrastructure), we mark as customer-attributed.
- Region failover: If Redwood performs an automated region failover (policy-configured), we exclude the short window used for DNS propagation (up to 120s) from SLO calculations. Longer propagation issues will be treated as incidents and handled per the crediting formula.

On credits and calculation examples (technical basis)
- Credits are calculated on the monthly invoice for the impacted resource pool. We compute the % of time the SLO target was missed in the month and apply the corresponding credit multiplier (see Karthik's commercial matrix).
- We include a 6-hour grace buffer for rolling deploys that affect <1% of traffic for <2 hours; this helps avoid credits for transient post-deploy instability.

Evidence and audit trail
- We can supply a small telemetry sample (redacted/sampled) and a dashboard snapshot showing the query counts, error counts, and percentiles for the 30-day window. I attached a sanitized sample telemetry file we can include.

I'll incorporate Marissa's legal phrasing once she suggests the precise exclusions for force majeure and third-party attribution.

Sooj

Hi Emily — attaching our consolidated response to the SLA section of your RFI plus supporting evidence. Summary bullets below; see attached PDF for the full questionnaire answers and examples.

Quick summary (high level)
- Measurement points: contractual availability and latency are measured at the service egress (edge return time) per-customer and per-region using a rolling 30-day window. P99 is the contractual latency metric.
- Latency baseline: For standard workloads (32-token footprint) our hosted tier targeted P99 is <= 700ms; for Dedicated pools we target P99 <= 300ms. We will surface separate sequence-length-normalized metrics for non-standard workloads.
- Availability targets & credits: Hosted API: 99.90% monthly availability. Dedicated (reserved) pools: 99.95%. Credits are tiered by % minutes below target in a calendar month; the maximum cumulative credit in a 12-month period is capped at 6 months of service fees for the impacted resource pool.
- Attribution and exclusions: We attribute incidents to Redwood when internal telemetry shows 5xx rates or internal timeouts tied to our runtime/gateway. We exclude synthetic probe traffic from contractual measurement and exclude scheduled maintenance windows communicated 72 hours in advance (for windows >15 minutes). Short DNS failovers (<=120s) caused by automated region failover are excluded.
- Sampling and telemetry integrity: We retain full-sample telemetry for long-tail analysis; where sampling is used the percentiles are corrected with Horvitz–Thompson weighting. We can provide a sanitized telemetry sample and dashboard exports for audit.

Next steps and asks from Atlas
1) Please confirm whether Atlas expects sequence-length-normalized measurement for your heavier workloads (we recommend enabling a separate SLO bucket if 75th percentile prompt length exceeds 64 tokens).
2) We'll prepare a redlined crediting paragraph for your legal team describing caps and force majeure language.
3) If acceptable, we can schedule a 30-minute technical review with Atlas SRE next week to walk telemetry examples and the sanitized evidence bundle.
